findings.label: Reason stated
findings.text: Voluntarily quit a job without good cause

findings.label: Sanction may end early if
findings.text: You become exempt from the work requirement; obtain a comparable new job; work 30+ hours/week; regain W-2 or unemployment eligibility; or the sanction period ends.

findings.label: Good cause
findings.text: The letter states that if you have a good cause reason for the job loss, there may be no loss of benefits. The agency decides.

findings.label: Exemptions listed in letter
findings.text: Under 16 or over 59; working 30+ hrs/week; caring for a child under 6 or a dependent unable to care for themselves; age 16–17 and not primary; AODA treatment; receiving/applied for unemployment insurance; enrolled half-time in school or training; physically or mentally unable to work; in certain work programs.

findings.label: Reapply date
findings.text: On or after 01/01/2027, or any time you become exempt. If part of a FoodShare group, contact the agency to update the case instead of reapplying.

findings.label: Fair hearing right
findings.text: You may request a fair hearing. Benefits may continue until a decision is made, but if the agency is found correct you may owe those benefits back. Free legal help: 1-888-278-0633.

tasks.text: Call Milwaukee Enrollment Services to report a good cause reason or a work-requirement exemption, and ask what proof is needed.
Request a fair hearing if you disagree with the sanction decision. Benefits may continue pending the decision, but may need to be repaid if the agency is upheld. Free legal help: 1-888-278-0633.

Gather any documents supporting a good cause reason (e.g., unsafe conditions, medical need, family care) or an exemption (e.g., proof of child's age, school enrollment, unemployment application). The agency will tell you exactly what is needed.
If the sanction period runs its course, reapply on or after 01/01/2027. If you are part of a FoodShare group, contact the agency to update the case instead.

FoodShare Notice of Sanction This letter is to notify you that you have voluntarily quit a job without good cause. As a result, you will not be eligible for FoodShare from 10/01/2026 to 12/31/2026. This sanction results in the total number of sanctions we have on ﬁle for you as: 1.

If you do not agree with this decision, you have the right to a fair hearing. You may be able to continue to get FoodShare beneﬁts until your fair hearing decision is made. If the fair hearing ofﬁcer decides that the agency was right, you may need to return the extra beneﬁts that you got after your beneﬁts were supposed to change. You may also be able to get free legal help. To learn more about free legal help, call 1-888-278-0633. Please see your beneﬁts letter for more details about ﬁling a fair hearing.
Your sanction may end if any of the following occurs:
You become exempt from the FoodShare work requirement.
You obtain a new job with pay or hours similar to the job you quit.
You work 30 or more hours per week.
You regain eligibility for W-2 by meeting the W-2 work requirements.
You regain eligibility for the unemployment beneﬁt by meeting the unemployment beneﬁt work requirements.
Your sanction period ends.

You will need to reapply for FoodShare if you want to get beneﬁts after your sanction period ends. You can reapply for beneﬁts any time on or after 01/01/2027 or any time you become exempt from the work requirement.
If you are part of a FoodShare group, you should contact your agency to update your case instead of reapplying.

PIN #: 0000000001 Date: 09/08/2026 Page 2 of 2 Work Registration All members of your FoodShare group must be registered for work unless they are exempt. You may be considered exempt and may not need to meet the FoodShare work requirement if any of the following applies to you:
You are younger than age 16 or older than age 59.
You are already working at least 30 hours per week (or getting weekly earnings that equal 30 times the federal minimum hourly wage).
You are the parent or are responsible for the care of a dependent child younger than age 6 (in or out of the home).
You are the parent or are responsible for the care of a person of any age who cannot care for himself or herself (in or out of the home).
You are age 16 or 17 and are not the primary person for the case.
You are taking part in an alcohol or other drug abuse (AODA) treatment program.
You are getting or have applied for unemployment insurance.
You are enrolled at least half-time in a recognized school, training program, or institution of higher learning.
You are physically or mentally unable to work.
You are taking part in certain work programs.

If you meet one of the exemptions listed above, you should contact your agency at the number listed at the top of page 1 of this letter to report the exemption and ﬁnd out what kind of proof may be needed.
If you have a good cause reason for the loss of job or hours, there may be no loss of FoodShare beneﬁts.
Questions If you have questions about this letter, contact your agency at the number listed at the top of page 1 of this letter.
